what: What predicts the Tier 3 fine-tune's gain: it is binary, not graded
law: A clip either LOCKS ON to its reference or it does not. If the fine-tune reduces the mean input error by >= 40%, it captures 98-117% of the headroom available to it. If the reduction is between 0 and 40%, it captures essentially nothing. If the input error grows, the clip gets worse. There is no middle band in 13 clips.
why_it_is_useful: Lock-on is measured from the input alone, so it needs no truth and can be read on Tier 2 and Tier 3 where truth-based selection is not permitted. Headroom says how much a clip has to give and needs truth, so it may choose which clips to RUN; lock-on says whether the clip collected it and is legal to read when choosing which rollout to SHIP. Together they predict a clip's contribution before it is scored against truth.

prediction_for_the_batch_in_flight.e01: already in: did not lock on (+6.30%), -2.42 cm
prediction_for_the_batch_in_flight.statement: e03 holds 48% of the batch's 284 cm of headroom, so the pre-registered -5 cm bar turns almost entirely on whether e03 locks on. If it does, e03 alone is about -4.5 cm on the 30-clip mean and the bar clears; if it does not, the batch lands near -1 cm and the registered answer is no upload. Written at 19:10 UTC, before e03 finishes training at ~19:40.

is_lock_on_predictable_in_advance.answer: No. Nothing available before the run predicts it.
is_lock_on_predictable_in_advance.hands: two-handed 5 of 9 locked on, one-handed 1 of 4 -- far too small to separate
is_lock_on_predictable_in_advance.counterexamples_that_kill_the_obvious_gu: A low reconstruction floor does not imply lock-on: e18 (3.88 cm), e08 (4.63) and e24 (8.94) all have excellent references and all went backwards. A high floor does not forbid it: e06 locked on at 26.21 cm. A large initial input error does not imply it either: e21 locked on from 116 cm while e17 did not from 99 cm.
is_lock_on_predictable_in_advance.planning_consequence: The arm is a lottery with measured odds and a measured payoff: lock-on happens about 54% of the time (7 of 13) and, when it does, collects ~100% of that clip's headroom. So the expected value of running one clip is about 0.54 x its headroom, and the ONLY lever is to pick the clips with the most headroom -- which is how e03, e25, e01, e29 and e16 were chosen. No cleverer pre-selection is available, and about $0.40 per clip is the price of finding out.

correction_2026_10_29_19_42.what_i_claimed: "A clip either locks on or it does not ... There is no middle band in 13 clips."
correction_2026_10_29_19_42.what_falsified_it: e03: input gain +48.78% (145.02 -> 74.28 cm), which is above the 40% threshold, yet it captured only 51% of its headroom (MPPE 150.88 -> 82.04 cm, -68.84 of a possible 135.36). Every earlier lock-on captured 98-117%.
correction_2026_10_29_19_42.revised_reading: Capture tracks the SIZE of the input gain, it is not a step function. Above about 57% gain the clip collects essentially all of its headroom; e03 at 49% collected half and e01 at 6% collected a tenth. Calling it binary was an artefact of having no clip between 6% and 57% -- e03 landed in that gap and filled it. The useful part survives: input gain is measurable without truth and predicts the realised gain, now as a magnitude rather than a flag.
correction_2026_10_29_19_42.why_i_am_recording_this: The binary claim was committed to a file 30 minutes before the clip that broke it finished training. Leaving it to stand would make every later number read as confirmation of a law that one of its own data points contradicts.

running_tally_of_the_batch.position: -2.98 cm of the -5 cm spending bar, and now genuinely live: e25 alone is -2.30 cm on the mean at full capture, which would clear it. second_correction_2026_10_29_20_12.what_i_claimed_at_19_42: that capture tracks the SIZE of the input gain -- 96% gain -> ~100% capture, 49% -> 51%, 6% -> 9%, which looked close to an identity.
second_correction_2026_10_29_20_12.what_falsified_it: e16: input gain only +11.02% (77.65 -> 69.09 cm) yet it captured 71% of its headroom (MPPE 67.24 -> 49.09 cm, -18.15 of a possible 25.57). e03 gained 49% and captured 51%; e16 gained 11% and captured 71%. The ordering is broken, so capture is not a function of input gain.
second_correction_2026_10_29_20_12.the_honest_statement: A high input gain is sufficient but not necessary. Above about 57% gain, 6 of 6 clips captured 98-117% of their headroom -- that half is solid. Below 57% the gain carries almost no information: gains of 6%, 11% and 49% produced captures of 9%, 71% and 51%. So the rule is one-directional, and I am not proposing a third functional form on nine points.
second_correction_2026_10_29_20_12.note_on_my_own_process: This is the second correction to the same claim in one afternoon. The first called it binary, the second called it proportional, and both were over-reading a small sample at the moment the data arrived. What survives both is narrow and worth keeping: a large input gain predicts a large realised gain, and nothing below that threshold predicts anything.
